title: work-orchestrator
summary: In use: my tool for keeping track of agents, tasks, and follow-ups.

links.label: Dika — taking the idea to a team

evidence: Checked against private code and work records. The benefits describe my own experience; time savings have not been measured.

story.label: Why I built it
story.text: Work gets scattered across chats, tasks, and pull requests. I don’t want to keep it all in my head.

story.label: Today
story.text: I use it to see what needs attention, pick up unfinished work, and follow up on reviews and checks. It helps me manage several agents without constantly rebuilding the context.

story.label: What I want
story.text: Less chasing updates. More time solving the actual problem.

title: Dika
summary: An idea for helping a team get work done with coding agents. Not built yet.
evidence: Checked against the private design, demo, and application records. Dika is a direction I want to pursue, not a tool a team is using yet.

story.label: The problem
story.text: Writing code is only part of the job. People still have to pass on context, chase reviews, and check that the change works.

story.label: Today
story.text: I’ve explored the idea with coding agents through research, design, and a demo. There is some starter code, but the product isn’t built yet.

story.label: What I want
story.text: A team can say what it needs, let agents do more of the work, and step in when a decision needs a person. Less passing work back and forth.
